summary: Root cause (top hypothesis H1, confidence 0.60, medium): payment-service's mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and was not renewed, so every call to bank-partner-api failed at the TLS handshake and fund transfers could not be executed. payment-service returned success-shaped (non-5xx) responses to callers, which is why the HTTP 5xx error-rate panel stayed flat (0.19-0.27%) while payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% and bank_api_error_rate went to 100%. The failure is localized to our own client-side certificate by 134 log lines naming the expired cert, pre-figured by a cert-watcher WARN at 11:50Z. Competing hypotheses (external bank outage H2 0.12, settlement deploy H3 0.06, timeout config H4 0.05, reporting artifact H5 0.02) are all contradicted or unsupported.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service's client mTLS certificate to bank-partner-api expired at 12:15Z, breaking all bank calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (owned by payment-service) reached its notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and was not renewed. From 12:14-12:15Z onward every call to bank-partner-api failed at the TLS handshake ('tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'), so fund transfers could not be executed. payment-service short-circuited these calls and returned success-shaped (non-5xx) responses to callers, which is why the HTTP 5xx error-rate panel stayed green while payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.5%. Category: credential_expiry — a time-based lifecycle event, not a deployment.

causal_chain.claim: The client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal was scheduled to expire at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and no renewal/rotation occurred in the change feeds.
Cert expiry at 12:15Z -> mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected; bank_api_error_rate jumps 0.2% -> 100% at 12:14Z.
Rejected handshakes -> transfers marked PENDING_RETRY / never settle; payment_success_rate collapses 99% -> ~2.5% from 12:20Z.
payment-service returns non-5xx to callers for these failed transfers, so HTTP error_rate stays flat at 0.19-0.27% (green dashboard) while absolute failures only surface as support tickets.
Failed calls fail fast rather than hang: p99 latency drops from ~320ms to ~140ms and request_rate stays ~100 req/s, matching short-circuited TLS failures.

assumptions: The cert-watcher WARN at 11:50Z (F12) and the 12:15:27Z PENDING_RETRY log (F11) are the same certificate named in the TLS alert; the log evidence is treated as one coherent signature.
Non-5xx status returned to callers for failed transfers is inferred from the flat HTTP error_rate (F10) plus collapsed success rate (F9); no direct status-code finding exists.
The absence of any credential/cert change in the config and deploy feeds (F15) reflects a genuine lack of renewal rather than monitoring gaps in those feeds.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner / PSP (bank-partner-api) degraded externally, breaking transfers
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api, the external bank/PSP connector, degraded on its own side (5xx / handshake-side failure), so payment-service's bank calls failed and transfers did not complete — matching the only exact historical precedent HIST-105 ('Payment failures: bank partner API outage', 2025-11-19). payment-service's HTTP error-rate panel stayed green because the failure occurred on outbound dependency calls, not inbound requests.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api degrades externally (no internal change in the 09:00-13:59Z window).
Degradation -> payment-service bank calls fail; bank_api_error_rate jumps 0.2% -> 100% at 12:14Z.
Failed bank calls -> transfers do not complete; payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%.
Outbound dependency failure is invisible to the inbound HTTP 5xx error-rate panel, explaining the green dashboard.

assumptions: The TLS 'expired certificate' errors observed could be attributed to the partner side if the alert were a server-certificate rejection, though the log text names OUR client cert and CN.
That bank-partner-api has an independent outage despite zero telemetry to confirm it.

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service v1.9.0 CSV exporter deployment (dep-5510) overloaded shared components, degrading payments
ranked_hypotheses.statement: settlement-service v1.9.0 'Batch settlement report export / new CSV exporter' deployed at 10:30Z overloaded a shared component in payment-service's graph (ledger-db, a shared postgres written by four services, or kafka, produced/consumed by four services), degrading payment-service's ability to complete transfers while leaving its inbound HTTP error rate flat. Precedent HIST-111 (a reporting job's full table scans slowed ledger-db).

causal_chain.claim: dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0, new CSV exporter) deploys at 10:30Z.
The exporter performs heavy reads/writes against the shared ledger-db and/or produces to shared kafka, saturating a fan-in point used by payment-service.
Shared-component contention -> payment-service transfers slow or stall -> payment_success_rate collapses.
Failure is at a dependency hop, so payment-service's inbound 5xx error_rate stays flat.

assumptions: The CSV exporter actually exercises shared components at volumes that affect other tenants.
No telemetry (db_pool_in_use, kafka lag, ledger-db latency) contradicting this was collected — resource/backlog metrics were never pulled (gap noted).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) broke or masked bank calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 11:20Z payment-service config change cfg-2502 raised bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000 after a 'partner advisory', and this change is the origin of the payment failures — either by letting calls hang longer or by interacting with a partner-side change. The 'partner advisory' hints an external condition coincided with the change window.

causal_chain.claim: A timeout increase could only lengthen waits for a slow/hanging partner, potentially converting failures into hangs or masking them.
This manifests as payment failures with normal HTTP error rate.

assumptions: That a pure timeout increase can cause (not merely mask) failed transfers.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-2502 is a timeout INCREASE (3s->5s), which can only make hung calls wait longer, yet latency actually DROPPED (~320ms -> ~140ms), consistent with fast short-circuits (F13, F18). It occurred 54-55 min before onset, no internal change aligns with the 12:14-12:15Z onset (F16), and the failure signature is an expired client certificate (F11), which no timeout value can produce.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Failures are external/client-side or a reporting artifact with no server-side anomaly
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The support lead's theory: the client app or the bank side is genuinely at fault, and there is no server-side anomaly — the ~40 tickets represent an absolute-volume blip masked by the error-rate denominator, or external failures not visible to server telemetry.

causal_chain.claim: Client app or bank side fails externally.
No server-side anomaly occurs, so payment-service's HTTP error-rate panel is correctly green.

assumptions: That externally observed failures leave no server-side signature.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Server-side telemetry shows a dramatic real anomaly: bank_api_error_rate 0.2% -> 100% (F8), payment_success_rate 99% -> 2.5% (F9), and 134 log lines naming an expired client certificate at the bank boundary (F11), pre-figured by a cert-watcher WARN at 11:50Z (F12). This is not an artifact and not purely external.

facts.statement: payment-service's client-side failure signature is an expired mTLS client certificate: 80x 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' and 54x 'marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (first 12:15:27Z).
A cert-watcher WARN at 2026-04-02T11:50:26Z pre-dated the failure, stating the client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal would expire in 25 minutes at notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z.
payment-service's bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 100% at 12:14Z and stayed at 100% through 12:30Z, versus a flat ~0.20% baseline from 11:00-12:12Z.
payment-service's payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% at 12:20Z and remained ~2.1-2.7% through 13:56Z.
payment-service HTTP error_rate (5xx) stayed flat at baseline (avg 0.19-0.27%, max 0.32%) for the entire window including the 12:12-12:28 onset buckets, explaining the green error-rate dashboard.

payment-service request_rate held steady (~90-110 req/s) and p99 latency actually DROPPED from ~320ms to ~138-144ms after 12:20Z, consistent with failed calls short-circuiting rather than hanging or saturating.
Exactly one deployment occurred across all services in 09:00-13:59Z: settlement-service v1.9.0 (dep-5510) at 10:30Z; no payment-service deployment exists in the window.
Exactly one config change occurred in the window: payment-service cfg-2502 raised bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000 at 11:20:00Z.
No certificate/credential/secret change or payment-service deployment appears anywhere in the 09:00-13:59Z config/deploy feeds.
cfg-2502 is a timeout increase (3000->5000ms), which can only mask hangs and cannot produce an expired-certificate failure; latency dropping rather than rising further excludes it as the mechanism.

bank-partner-api has no directly observable telemetry (type external, has_telemetry:false); it can only be observed through its callers, so no independent signal exists to attribute the failure to the bank side.
The only exact historical symptom match (HIST-105, external bank 5xx) does not match; the closer precedent is HIST-106 (mTLS certificate expired, credential_expiry).

assumptions: The cert-watcher WARN at 11:50Z (F12) and the 12:15:27Z PENDING_RETRY/TLS-alert logs (F11) refer to the same certificate named in the TLS alert; the log evidence is treated as one coherent signature.
The non-5xx status returned to callers for failed transfers is inferred from the flat HTTP error_rate (F10) plus the collapsed success rate (F9); no direct status-code finding exists.
The absence of any credential/cert change in the config and deploy feeds (F15) reflects a genuine lack of renewal rather than monitoring gaps in those feeds.

recommended_actions.action: Renew/rotate the payment-service mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) via the credential/cert provisioning path, then restart/reload payment-service so the new cert is loaded, and verify bank_api_error_rate returns to its ~0.2% baseline and payment_success_rate recovers to ~99%.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the specific expired credential identified at the failure boundary; every bank call fails at the TLS handshake until it is replaced.

recommended_actions.action: While the renewal is in flight, treat the bank-call failures as intentional fail-fast: confirm payment-service is not silently returning success-shaped responses to customers for failed transfers, and switch it to an explicit error/queued-retry path so failed transfers are visible rather than masked.
recommended_actions.rationale: The success-shaped non-5xx responses kept the 5xx error-rate panel green and hid the outage from monitoring.

recommended_actions.action: Add a direct alert on payment_success_rate (and bank_api_error_rate) with a threshold well above the ~2.5% collapse, so a success-rate drop pages even when HTTP 5xx error_rate is flat.
recommended_actions.rationale: The existing error-rate-only panel is blind to outbound-dependency short-circuits; success rate is the metric that actually moved.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the fix end-to-end after renewal: re-check bank_api_error_rate returns to ~0.2%, payment_success_rate to ~99%, and PENDING_RETRY log volume drops to zero over a full window (e.g. 30-60 minutes).
recommended_actions.rationale: Confirms the expiry was the sole mechanism and that no residual handshake failures remain.

recommended_actions.action: Implement certificate lifecycle automation for payment-service: enforce alerting and auto-renewal well before notAfter (the cert-watcher fired only 25 minutes before expiry at 11:50Z), and gate renewals through change management so an unmanaged expiry cannot recur.
recommended_actions.rationale: No credential/secret change appeared in the change feeds and the 25-minute warning was not acted on; the gap is in renewal management, not in a deployment.

recommended_actions.action: Add a synthetic/external probe that exercises the full bank transfer path (including the mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api) and alerts on failure, since bank-partner-api exposes no telemetry and can only be observed through its callers.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partner has no directly observable metrics/logs, so detection must come from caller-side end-to-end checks.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api exposes no telemetry (type external, has_telemetry:false; a direct metrics query returned not_found), so the partner's own health and certificate state cannot be measured and can only be inferred through payment-service's client-side bank_api_error_rate.

No queries were possible for network changes, feature-flag flips, or credential/secret rotations in 09:00-13:59Z; absence of such changes is unverified rather than proven. The mechanism by which the cert reached expiry without renewal is not visible in the change record.

Could not query sibling/caller services (e.g. api-gateway) or bank-partner-api logs due to budget_exhausted, so the blast radius beyond payment-service is unknown and propagated errors/latency in callers are unverified.

Did not retrieve timeout counts, queue/backlog depth, db_pool_in_use, cpu_pct/memory_pct, or restart counts before budget exhaustion; saturation/hang/backlog hypotheses (H3) are not fully ruled out by resource metrics, though flat request_rate and falling latency argue against them.
Historical precedent search returned only 6 incidents (limit 6) and was not flagged truncated; other credential-expiry or config-change cases for payment-service may exist beyond the returned set.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that the TLS 'expired certificate' alert referred to the bank-partner-api's server certificate rather than our client certificate, or that bank-partner-api was independently failing (e.g. partner-side telemetry showing 5xx or its own cert expiry), which would shift the conclusion toward H2.

A credential/secret rotation into the bank connector appearing in the change feeds at or near 12:14-12:15Z, which would indicate an internal change mechanism rather than an unmanaged time-based expiry.

Persistence of bank_api_error_rate at 100% and payment_success_rate at ~2.5% after the client certificate is renewed and reloaded — this would show the expired cert is not the (sole) cause and re-open external/dependency hypotheses.
Resource telemetry (db_pool_in_use saturation, kafka lag, ledger-db latency spikes) temporally aligned with 12:14-12:15Z, which would support the shared-component/deployment hypothesis H3.
Direct status-code evidence showing payment-service returned 5xx (rather than success-shaped responses) during the outage, which would weaken the masking explanation for the green error-rate panel.
